Actually we should check if area quadrilateral = area(ABC) - area(AKB) - area(AKL) - area(ALC) indeed holds. Let's test with approximate numbers from earlier (x=y approx 26.845 => a=b≈13.4225, p≈3.937, q≈3.937). Compute area(ABC) = 2ab = 2*(13.4225)*(13.4225) = 2*180.5 = 361.0 (makes sense because area = (1/2)*x*y = (1/2)*(2a)*(2b) = 2ab, and a^2+b^2=361, but a=b, so a^2 = b^2 = 180.5 => ab = 180.5? Actually a=b=13.4225, then ab = (13.4225)^2 = 180.5, so area=2*180.5=361. So area(ABC) = 361. area(AKB)=a p=13.4225*3.937≈53.03. area(ALC)=b q same ≈53.03. area(AKL)=49*1.732...=49*1.732=84.868 approx. So area quadrilateral = 361 - 53.03 - 53.03 - 84.87 = 170.07. That matches earlier approximate area ~173.1 (some difference due to approximations). So seems consistent. So area quadrilateral = 2ab - a p - b q - 49 sqrt(3) is correct.
